source_metadata.title: Adjuvant Palbociclib for Early Breast Cancer: The PALLAS Trial Results (ABCSG-42/AFT-05/BIG-14-03)
source_metadata.authors_display: Michael Gnant et al., on behalf of the PALLAS groups and investigators
source_metadata.source_type: prospective multicenter randomized open-label phase III clinical trial
source_metadata.appendix_pages: PDF pages 15-25, investigator and site roster

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Primary PALLAS trial methods, population, main efficacy endpoints, Table 2 event categories, all Figure 3 subgroup hazard ratios, treatment exposure, key safety findings, funding, disclosures, data sharing, and author conclusions were atomized. Secondary-study claims in the Discussion and bibliography were not converted into primary-study findings.

atoms.canonical_statement: PALLAS tested whether adding adjuvant palbociclib to standard endocrine therapy improves outcomes compared with endocrine therapy alone in early hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: designed to determine whether the addition of palbociclib to standard adjuvant endocrine therapy improves outcomes

atoms.canonical_statement: PALLAS was a prospective, multicenter, randomized, open-label phase III trial conducted at 406 centers in 21 countries on five continents.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: prospective, multicenter, randomized open-label phase III trial was conducted in 406 centers in 21 countries

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible participants were age 18 years or older with histologically confirmed stage II or III hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: histologically confirmed stage II or III hormone receptor-positive breast cancer and age 18 years or older

population.label: Eligible adults with stage II or III hormone receptor-positive breast cancer
inclusion_criteria: Histologically confirmed stage II or III hormone receptor-positive breast cancer

atoms.canonical_statement: Before randomization, participants had completed definitive breast surgery and chemotherapy or radiotherapy when indicated; endocrine therapy had to start within 12 months of diagnosis and enrollment within 6 months of starting endocrine therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: completed definitive breast surgery ... enrollment into the study had to occur within 6 months of starting endocrine therapy

population.label: Timing and prior-treatment eligibility
inclusion_criteria: Endocrine therapy started within 12 months of diagnosis
Enrollment within 6 months of endocrine therapy start

atoms.canonical_statement: Absence of metastatic disease had to be established before randomization, and receipt of a tumor tissue block at a central biorepository was mandatory.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Lack of metastatic disease had to be proven ... receipt of a tumor tissue block ... was mandatory

population.label: Nonmetastatic disease with mandatory tissue submission
inclusion_criteria: Tumor tissue block received by central biorepository

atoms.canonical_statement: Participants were randomized 1:1 using permuted blocks of size 4 or 6, stratified by anatomic stage, prior neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy, age, and geographic region.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: permuted block design with random block size (4 or 6) was used to randomly assign the patients 1:1

atoms.canonical_statement: The intervention was palbociclib 125 mg orally once daily on days 1-21 of a 28-day cycle for 2 years plus standard adjuvant endocrine therapy for at least 5 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: palbociclib at a starting dose of 125 mg orally once daily, days 1-21 ... for a total duration of 2 years

exposures.frequency: once daily on days 1-21 of each 28-day cycle
exposures.details: Endocrine therapy continued for at least 5 years.

atoms.canonical_statement: The protocol allowed palbociclib dose reductions to 100 mg and 75 mg and treatment interruptions, with discontinuation required for repeated grade 3 or higher neutropenia.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: allowed for palbociclib dose reductions (to 100 mg and 75 mg ...), and interruptions, with discontinuation required for repeated severe neutropenia

atoms.canonical_statement: The comparator was standard adjuvant endocrine therapy alone for at least 5 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Patients randomly assigned to arm B received endocrine therapy alone for a duration of at least 5 years

atoms.canonical_statement: Both groups underwent physical examination and laboratory testing at least quarterly for 2 years, then every 6 months through year 5 and annually through year 10; imaging was symptom-directed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: evaluated by physical examination and laboratory testing at least quarterly for the first 2 years ... Any imaging was symptom-directed

atoms.canonical_statement: Invasive disease-free survival was a primary endpoint.

outcome.definition: Time from randomization to first local or regional invasive ipsilateral recurrence, contralateral invasive breast cancer, distant recurrence, second primary invasive nonbreast cancer, or death from any cause

atoms.canonical_statement: Invasive breast cancer-free survival was a secondary endpoint.

outcome.definition: Secondary time-to-event endpoint defined using updated STEEP criteria

atoms.canonical_statement: Distant recurrence-free survival was a secondary endpoint.
Locoregional recurrence-free survival was a secondary endpoint.
Overall survival was a secondary endpoint.
The final iDFS analysis was designed around a target hazard ratio of 0.75, 469 events, 85% power, and a one-sided type I error rate of 0.025 using a group-sequential design.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 469 events had to occur to achieve a power of 85% in the final analysis

atoms.canonical_statement: The design included two interim analyses. At the second interim analysis, the test statistic crossed the prespecified futility boundary and palbociclib was stopped in about 350 patients still receiving it on May 29, 2020.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: crossed the predefined futility boundary and palbociclib was discontinued in the approximately 350 patients

atoms.canonical_statement: The primary analysis followed intention-to-treat principles. Time-to-event comparisons used stratified log-rank tests, Kaplan-Meier estimates, and stratified Cox models with two-sided 95% confidence intervals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: According to the intention-to-treat principle ... Stratified log-rank tests ... Kaplan-Meier curves ... HRs with two-sided 95% CIs

atoms.canonical_statement: Post hoc analyses used unstratified Cox models for subgroup comparisons and examined treatment-effect heterogeneity and the relation of palbociclib exposure, dose reductions, and early discontinuation to iDFS.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Further post hoc analyses investigated treatment effect heterogeneity and the possible impact of drug exposure in relation to iDFS

atoms.canonical_statement: Safety analyses used patients who started palbociclib or endocrine therapy, classified by actual treatment received, and summarized treatment-emergent toxicities by maximum grade.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Safety analyses were performed ... according to actual treatment received. Incidences of treatment-emergent toxicities were reported

atoms.canonical_statement: Pfizer provided study drug and financial support. The academic groups ABCSG and AFT also supported the trial with human resources.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The trial was funded by Pfizer, who provided study drug and financial support

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors reported that the funder had no role in data collection, data analysis, or data interpretation.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The funder had no role in data collection, data analysis, or data interpretation

atoms.canonical_statement: Of 5,796 randomized participants, 35 withdrew consent for use of all data, leaving 5,761 in the intention-to-treat population: 2,884 assigned to palbociclib plus endocrine therapy and 2,877 to endocrine therapy alone.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 35 withdrew consent for use of all data, resulting in 5,761 patients included in the intention-to-treat population

exposures.details: Endocrine therapy continued for at least 5 years.

atoms.canonical_statement: The median age was 52 years with an interquartile range of 45-61 years.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: median age was 52 years (interquartile range, 45-61 years)

atoms.canonical_statement: Most participants had stage IIB or III disease: 4,728 of 5,761, or 82.1%.
Neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy had been given to 4,754 of 5,761 participants, or 82.5%.
Postmenopausal participants comprised 3,096 of 5,761, or 53.7%, and 36 participants, or 0.6%, were male.
At treatment initiation, 3,872 participants, or 67.2%, received an aromatase inhibitor; 1,872, or 32.5%, received tamoxifen; and 1,243, or 21.6%, received concurrent ovarian function suppression.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that adding adjuvant palbociclib to standard endocrine therapy did not improve outcomes compared with endocrine therapy alone in early hormone receptor-positive breast cancer.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the addition of adjuvant palbociclib to standard endocrine therapy did not improve outcomes

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors reported that landmark analyses did not identify suboptimal palbociclib exposure as the reason for the lack of efficacy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: landmark analyses did not reveal suboptimal drug exposure as a reason for the observed lack of palbociclib efficacy

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors proposed translational analyses of the trans-PALLAS biospecimen program and long-term follow-up to investigate biomarkers and possible explanations for the lack of adjuvant palbociclib benefit.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: translational science will help to better understand unique tissue and/or serum biomarkers
